title: Things to Do in Supetar, Croatia: Top Attractions 2027
metaDescription: Top things to do in Supetar, Brač: St. Peter's Church, the Petrinović Mausoleum, Banj beach, the Riva and the Split ferry, with prices in euros.
content:
## Why Supetar Is Worth More Than a Ferry Stop

Supetar is the largest town on Brač and its main port, with a compact stone-built centre, a long waterfront and several pebble beaches. Most visitors arrive on the Jadrolinija car ferry from Split. The crossing takes about 50 minutes and costs €6.50 per adult in high season. Fares are lower off season. Children aged 3–12 pay €3.20 in high season.

The town works well on foot. Everything in this guide sits within about 1.5 km of the port, so a car is not needed for the main sights.

## Top Attractions in Supetar

### Petrinović Mausoleum

The Petrinović Mausoleum is the most important single sight in Supetar. It stands on the Glavica peninsula in the town cemetery, a short walk west of the centre. The sculptor Toma Rosandić designed it in the 1920s for the Petrinović family, who were wealthy local emigrants. The building is made of white Brač stone and has a Neo-Byzantine look. Its front shows a strict, symmetrical composition with a domed top.

The cemetery is open to visitors and entry is free. Visit in the late afternoon, when the stone turns warm and the sun is lower. Dress modestly, because it is an active burial ground.

### Parish Church of St. Peter

St. Peter's is the town's namesake church (Supetar comes from the Latin name of St. Peter). It sits close to the harbour. The church has a distinctive bell tower and a plain, stone-faced interior. The church is usually open for short visits outside service times. Entry is free and donations are welcome. Shoulders and knees should be covered.

### The Riva Waterfront

The Riva is a wide promenade that follows the harbour and is the centre of Supetar's social life. It has cafés, ice-cream counters, small shops and a row of moored boats. It is flat and easy for strollers and wheelchairs. The busiest time is the evening, after about 19:00, when locals and visitors walk the full length. For the quietest coffee, go before 09:30.

### Old Town Streets

Behind the Riva, a handful of narrow lanes hold stone houses, small squares and a few shops that sell local olive oil, wine and Brač stone souvenirs. The old core is small and can be walked in 30–45 minutes at an easy pace.

## Best Beaches in Supetar

Supetar's beaches are mainly pebble and concrete platforms, with clear, calm water. Sea temperature is about 24–26°C in July and August. It is around 18–20°C in late May and early October.

### Banj Beach

Banj is the best-known town beach. It is a pebble beach close to the centre with shallow water and a family-friendly layout. Showers, cafés, sunbed rental and a small play area are close by. It gets busy from about 11:00 to 16:00 in July and August. Arrive before 10:00 for a spot with space.

### Vlačica Beach

Vlačica is on the other side of the centre. It is a smaller pebble bay with a quieter feel than Banj. It is suitable for swimming with children and for a short walk back to town for lunch.

### Sv. Nikola Peninsula

The Sv. Nikola peninsula (Rt Sv. Nikola) is a green headland with pine trees. It has shaded paths and rocky platforms for swimming. A walk around it takes about 30–40 minutes. It is the best option for anyone who wants shade rather than a beach with services. Bring water shoes, because the entry points are rocky.

## Top Activities in Supetar

### Swimming and Water Sports

Several operators along the main beaches rent stand-up paddleboards, kayaks and pedal boats in summer. Expect roughly €10–15 per hour for a paddleboard or kayak, and slightly more for a pedal boat. Prices vary by operator and season, so check on the spot. Mornings usually have the calmest sea.

### Walking and Cycling Along the Coast

A flat coastal path runs along the shoreline from the centre toward the beaches and the Sv. Nikola headland. Bike rental is widely available in town. Expect about €15–25 for a day. Cycling along the coast road is easy in spring and autumn. In July and August, heat makes midday rides unpleasant.

### Eating Local Dishes

Supetar's konobas and harbour restaurants serve grilled fish, black risotto, octopus salad and Dalmatian pašticada. Brač lamb and local olive oil are the island's signature products. The island's best-known cheese is a sheep milk cheese in oil called Brački sir. Mains at harbour restaurants generally cost €15–25, and grilled fresh fish is sold by weight, typically €60–90 per kilogram. Ask for the weight and price before ordering.

### Evening Life

The evening is the main event. Bars on the Riva stay open late in July and August, and there are occasional open-air concerts and local festivals in summer. The town is calmer than Hvar or Makarska, which is the main reason many families choose it.

## How to Get to Supetar

| Route | Time | Price |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Jadrolinija car ferry Split–Supetar | About 50 min | €6.50 per adult; about €26.10 per car in high season |
| Krilo (Kapetan Luka) catamaran Split–Supetar | About 20–25 min | About €10 per person, foot passengers only |

The car ferry runs from about 05:00 until just before midnight, with up to 14 sailings a day in high season, and it is the most flexible choice. The catamaran is faster but has fewer departures and does not carry cars.

## Local Tips for Visiting Supetar

- **Skip the car in summer.** A vehicle on the ferry adds about €26 each way, and parking in the centre is limited in July and August. Walking covers everything in this guide.
- **Buy ferry tickets early in peak season.** Queues at the Split port can be long at weekends, mostly on Friday evenings and Sunday afternoons.
- **Time the mausoleum visit for late day.** Light is better and the cemetery is quieter.
- **Choose Vlačica or Sv. Nikola over Banj in high season.** They are quieter at midday.
- **Eat away from the first row of tables.** One street back from the Riva, prices are often lower and menus are more local.
- **Visit in late May, June or September.** The sea is warm, crowds are smaller and accommodation is cheaper than in July and August.

## How Much Time to Spend

A half day is enough to see the mausoleum, St. Peter's and the Riva and to have a swim. A full day adds the Sv. Nikola walk and a long lunch. Two or three nights lets the town work at a slower pace. The clear recommendation is to stay at least one night rather than treating Supetar as a pass-through: the town is at its best in the evening, after the day-trip groups have left.

## Best Time to Visit

July and August are hottest, with daytime highs of about 30°C and the liveliest evenings. May, June and September offer the best balance of warm water, lighter crowds and lower prices. Between November and March many seasonal restaurants and rental shops close, though the ferry runs all year.

## Practical Information

- **Currency:** euro (€).
- **Language:** Croatian; English is widely spoken in tourist businesses.
- **Bus connection:** buses to other Brač towns leave from the station beside the ferry port, timed around ferry arrivals.
- **Pharmacy and supermarkets:** available in the centre, with the main supermarkets a short walk from the port.
- **Swimming safety:** sea urchins live on rocky entries, so water shoes are worth carrying.

faq.question: What is the best thing to do in Supetar?
faq.answer: The Petrinović Mausoleum is the top cultural sight, and a walk along the Riva at sunset is the best general experience. Both are free and can be done within a couple of hours.

faq.question: How do I get from Split to Supetar?
faq.answer: The Jadrolinija car ferry takes about 50 minutes and costs €6.50 per adult in high season. The Krilo catamaran is faster at roughly 20–25 minutes and costs about €10, but it carries foot passengers only.

faq.question: Is Supetar worth visiting?
faq.answer: Yes, for a relaxed stay with beaches, a walkable centre and a calm evening scene. It is less crowded than Hvar or Makarska. It is not the place for dramatic scenery, which is found elsewhere on the island.

faq.question: What are the best beaches in Supetar?
faq.answer: Banj is the best-known and has the most services, while Vlačica is smaller and quieter. The pine-covered Sv. Nikola peninsula is the best choice for shade and rock swimming.

faq.question: How many days do you need in Supetar?
faq.answer: One full day covers the main sights and a swim. Two or three nights suit travellers who want beach time, a coastal walk and evenings on the Riva.

faq.question: Do you need a car in Supetar?
faq.answer: No. The main sights and beaches are within about 1.5 km of the ferry port and are easy to reach on foot. A car costs about €26.10 on the ferry in high season and is only useful for exploring the rest of Brač.

faq.question: When is the best time to visit Supetar?
faq.answer: Late May, June and September offer warm water, fewer people and lower prices. July and August are hotter and livelier but also the busiest and most expensive.

quickAnswer: The top things to do in Supetar are the Petrinović Mausoleum, the parish church of St. Peter, the Riva waterfront, swimming at Banj and the pine-shaded Sv. Nikola peninsula, plus water sports and evening dining. Most sights are free and within 1.5 km of the ferry port.
